source.title: Initial Guessing Bias: How Untrained Networks Favor Some Classes
source.authors: Emanuele Francazi; Aurélien Lucchi; Marco Baity-Jesi

record.file_problem: Full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures how initial prediction imbalance relates to training accuracy over time, using different architectures and data preprocessing settings. This bears conceptually on training from initialization, but it does not measure whether training classification error reaches zero.
record.gate_note: The study's main results concern initial guessing bias and its relationship to accuracy during training. It reports no exact training-error values or explicit zero-error result. Rows below record the text-described training-dynamics results; plotted values are not reconstructed.
record.test_reason: The study establishes initial guessing bias and measures its absorption during early training. Its reported finding is slower convergence under greater bias, not whether sufficiently large CNNs reach near-zero training error. Input shifts do not test activation-matched weight initialization, and the study provides no comparisons testing V2–V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate, with one qualification: the authors tentatively infer limited effects on final convergence from IGB's presence in successful architectures; they do not establish this through a systematic final-error comparison. Their experiments show greater IGB delaying bias absorption and accuracy improvement on balanced data, while broader benefits and harms remain unresolved.
record.recipe_differences: Measures initial prediction fractions and training accuracy over time, with IGB adjusted by input shifts; it does not directly evaluate the zero-training-error outcome in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: The level of IGB varies with data standardization and differs across architectures; the text says higher IGB increases absorption time and slows convergence.

fits_no_version.finding: Increasing input offsets increases initial guessing bias and delays its absorption, slowing accuracy improvement on balanced binary CIFAR and CIFAR-10 across ResNet34, ViT and MLP-mixer.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Greater initial prediction imbalance can slow early gradient-based training on balanced classification datasets.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning, Proceedings of the 41st International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 235 (2024)
record.problems: The training-dynamics results are described qualitatively and shown in figures without exact values in the text. The authors say the experiments are representative rather than exhaustive; they do not report exact final training errors for these settings.
record.rows_left_out: No rows for the CIFAR10/CIFAR100 initial-guessing-bias histograms: those measure initialization predictions, not a training outcome named by the versions. No training-dynamics rows for test accuracy, since the version concerns training error.

untested.parts: Attainment of zero or near-zero training classification error in sufficiently large CNNs; random or corrupted labels; size, optimizer, early-stopping and regularization qualifications.
Teacher-student ReLU optimization, spurious local minima and the effect of extra student neurons.
Training-error degradation with depth, identity-shortcut comparisons and special initialization alternatives.
Activation-matched initialization effects on training speed and trainable depth; orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization and orthogonal convolution kernels.
Learning rates relative to stability thresholds, curvature dynamics, recovery and divergence.
Batch-normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: The V1 limits_scope label should be removed: slower convergence alone does not qualify a claim about eventual near-zero training error. Depth-dependent IGB and batch-normalization analogies concern different outcomes from V3, V4 and V6.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test zero or near-zero training classification error, corrupted or random labels, model size thresholds, SGD versus Adam comparisons, smaller models, early stopping, or regularized recipes.

relation.reason: The study discusses initialization, signal propagation and training dynamics, but its own results address a different construct from the claim versions.

tranche.reason: The experiments measure initial guessing bias and its absorption during training. They do not establish near-zero final training error or test the comparisons specified by V2–V6.

source_check.notes: Higher IGB slows bias absorption and accuracy improvement on balanced data; exact endpoint accuracies are not stated. Appendix I.2's suggestion of limited effects on final convergence is tentative.
